title: Vinod Khosla Says AI Is Creating a ‘Hyperabundance’ of New Drugs, but Testing Is Still ‘18th-Century’

content_html:

Venture capitalist Vinod Khosla said artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding drug discovery, but traditional testing methods have failed to keep pace with the technology's progress.

AI and Human Tissue Drug Testing

On Wednesday, in a post on X, Khosla said AI has produced what he described as a "21st-century hyperabundance of potential new drugs and biological hypotheses," while drug testing still relies heavily on conventional animal studies.

He argued that the industry needs a more human-relevant approach to evaluating potential treatments.

"We are still using 18th-century style animal testing," Khosla wrote.

He pointed to Vivodyne, a biotechnology company developing technology to test drugs using living human tissues at scale.

"Instead, @Vivodyne is evaluating drugs in living human tissues at industrial scale," Khosla said.

He also said he was excited to continue working with Vivodyne as the company develops its "Virtual Human" data center, which he said could eventually help researchers predict how patients will respond to treatments.

AI has created a 21st-century hyperabundance of potential new drugs and biological hypotheses, but we are still using 18th-century style animal testing.

Instead, @Vivodyne is evaluating drugs in living human tissues at industrial scale.

— Vinod Khosla (@vkhosla) August 12, 2026

AI Accelerates Drug Discovery and Healthcare

Earlier, Anthropic, Takeda Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., Nvidia Corp. and Eli Lilly and Co. highlighted the growing role of AI in drug discovery and medical research.

Anthropic launched Claude Science, an AI workbench that combined scientific literature analysis, computational biology, code generation and large-scale computing, with access to more than 60 scientific skills and connectors

Takeda reported that its AI-developed psoriasis drug zasocitinib significantly outperformed Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.'s Sotyktu in a Phase 3 trial, with more than 35% of patients achieving complete skin clearance at week 16.

Meanwhile, Nvidia and Eli Lilly announced a $1 billion AI co-innovation lab aimed at combining AI with biological research to accelerate drug development.

风险投资家 Vinod Khosla 表示，人工智能 (AI) 正在迅速扩大药物发现，但传统的测试方法未能跟上技术进步的步伐。

人工智能和人体组织药物测试

周三，科斯拉在 X 上发表的一篇文章中表示，人工智能已经产生了他所说的“21 世纪大量的潜在新药和生物学假设”，而药物测试仍然严重依赖传统的动物研究。

他认为该行业需要一种更与人相关的方法来评估潜在的治疗方法。

“我们仍在使用 18 世纪风格的动物测试，”科斯拉写道。

他提到了 Vivodyne，这是一家生物技术公司，开发利用活体人体组织大规模测试药物的技术。

“相反，@Vivodyne 正在以工业规模评估活体人体组织中的药物，”科斯拉说。

他还表示，他很高兴继续与 Vivodyne 合作，因为该公司正在开发“虚拟人类”数据中心，他表示该数据中心最终可以帮助研究人员预测患者对治疗的反应。

人工智能加速药物发现和医疗保健

此前，Anthropic、武田药品工业株式会社。 有限公司、Nvidia 公司和礼来公司。 强调了人工智能在药物发现和医学研究中日益重要的作用。

Anthropic 推出了 Claude Science，这是一个结合了科学文献分析、计算生物学、代码生成和大规模计算的 AI 工作台，可访问 60 多种科学技能和连接器

武田报告称，其 AI 开发的牛皮癣药物 zasocitinib 在 3 期试验中显着优于百时美施贵宝公司的 Sotyktu，超过 35% 的患者在第 16 周时实现了皮肤完全清除。

与此同时，英伟达和礼来公司宣布斥资 10 亿美元成立人工智能联合创新实验室，旨在将人工智能与生物研究相结合，加速药物开发。
